headline: Malaysia to hire 200,000 Bangladeshi workers in next six months
summary: The recruitment process will begin in phases from late September, with 10,000 workers to be hired free of cost.
details: Malaysia will recruit approximately 200,000 workers from Bangladesh over the next six months, according to State Minister for LGRD and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam.
The recruitment process is set to begin in phases starting from the end of September and will be implemented through various agencies in the country.
Out of the total 200,000 workers, 10,000 will be hired free of cost, the state minister added.
Beyond manpower, preparations are underway for Malaysia to invest about US$2 billion in Bangladesh's electric vehicles, solar panels, renewable energy, and halal food sectors.
These announcements followed a meeting between Malaysian High Commissioner Mohd Shuhada Othman and LGRD and Cooperatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan.
The meeting also touched upon the registration of unregistered Bangladeshi workers currently in Malaysia, where about 8 lakh workers are already registered.
Additionally, discussions were held regarding the visit of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to Malaysia to further strengthen bilateral relations.
caption:
200,000 jobs in Malaysia! 🇲🇾

Recruitment for Bangladeshi workers begins this September.

Malaysia will recruit approximately 200,000 workers from Bangladesh over the next six months, according to State Minister for LGRD and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam.

The recruitment process is set to begin in phases starting from the end of September and will be implemented through various agencies in the country.

Out of the total 200,000 workers, 10,000 will be hired free of cost, the state minister added.

Beyond manpower, preparations are underway for Malaysia to invest about US$2 billion in Bangladesh's electric vehicles, solar panels, renewable energy, and halal food sectors.

These announcements followed a meeting between Malaysian High Commissioner Mohd Shuhada Othman and LGRD and Cooperatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan.

The meeting also touched upon the registration of unregistered Bangladeshi workers currently in Malaysia, where about 8 lakh workers are already registered.

Additionally, discussions were held regarding the visit of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to Malaysia to further strengthen bilateral relations.

headline_marked: Dhaka to [[ban battery-powered rickshaws on main roads]] to curb traffic
headline: Dhaka to ban battery-powered rickshaws on main roads to curb traffic
summary: Authorities are targeting battery-run auto-rickshaws to reduce accidents, traffic congestion, and power theft in the capital.
details: Battery-powered rickshaws will be banned from operating on the main roads of Dhaka to address growing concerns over safety and traffic flow.
The move comes as these vehicles are frequently linked to road accidents and severe traffic jams across the city.
Beyond traffic issues, authorities have highlighted the problem of power theft, as many of these vehicles are charged using illegal electricity connections.
The government is currently working on a framework to regulate battery-run auto-rickshaws to ensure they do not disrupt urban mobility.
State ministers have indicated that while regulation is the goal, the immediate priority is removing them from major thoroughfares to ease congestion.
caption:
No more battery-run rickshaws on Dhaka's main roads. The city is cracking down to stop traffic jams and power theft.

Battery-powered rickshaws will be banned from operating on the main roads of Dhaka to address growing concerns over safety and traffic flow.

The move comes as these vehicles are frequently linked to road accidents and severe traffic jams across the city.

Beyond traffic issues, authorities have highlighted the problem of power theft, as many of these vehicles are charged using illegal electricity connections.

The government is currently working on a framework to regulate battery-run auto-rickshaws to ensure they do not disrupt urban mobility.

State ministers have indicated that while regulation is the goal, the immediate priority is removing them from major thoroughfares to ease congestion.
